fields.rationale: States cluster around whether they require the other state to reciprocate in kind (mutual recognition), accept equivalent standards without a formal mutual-reciprocity clause, hinge reciprocity primarily on waiving the exam under specific conditions, use an endorsement framework with additional criteria, restrict reciprocity to a narrow license type or project, or offer a streamlined universal-recognition pathway.

assignments.raw_value: Applicant must be currently licensed in a reciprocating state that recognizes, at minimum, Alabama's standards, and must pay prescribed fees.
Applicant must be currently licensed as a master or journeyman plumber in another state whose plumbing laws and codes are similar to those of Arkansas.

Applicant must hold a license in good standing in another state that has reciprocal acceptance of California qualifications; board determines on a case-by-case basis that the other state's qualifications are at least equivalent to California's. Trade examination may be waived if applicant provides written certification that their out-of-state license has been in good standing for the previous five years.

Applicant must hold a license in good standing in another jurisdiction and demonstrate substantially equivalent credentials and qualifications. Board may require a 6-month waiting period after issuance of out-of-state license.
Applicant must hold a similar license from another state with substantially similar or higher requirements, and that state must grant reciprocal licensure to CT licensees without examination.

Proof of current licensure in good standing in another state, DC, or US territory with substantially similar standards, plus submission of verified evidence per § 1808(a)(3)-(5). If standards are not substantially similar, applicant must have practiced for a minimum of 7 years after licensure.

Applicant must meet FL certification requirements and have passed a substantially equivalent exam, OR hold a valid license from another state with substantially equivalent criteria, OR hold a valid license from a state with a reciprocal agreement, OR have held a valid license from another state for at least 10 years.
Reciprocity available where other states have requirements substantially equal to Georgia's requirements and offer a similar privilege to Georgia residents.

Licensure by endorsement or reciprocity available; expedited for nonresident military spouses who can demonstrate competency in lieu of work-experience time requirement. General reciprocity/endorsement pathway available under the umbrella Professional and Vocational Licensing Act.

Nonresident applicant must be licensed under plumbing statutes of another state with similar licensing requirements, and that state must grant the same reciprocal licensing privileges to Iowa residents. Board may license without examination.

Applicant must be at least 21 years of age, and the Board must find that the requirements for registration or licensing of plumbers in such other state or municipality were substantially equal to Illinois requirements at the date of registration or license, and that the same privilege of registration is accorded by said state or municipality to Illinois licensed plumbers. Alternatively, if no reciprocal agreement exists, the applicant may obtain an Illinois license by passing the Illinois plumber's examination and paying required fees.

Applicant must be licensed/registered in another state, territory, country, or province in the same category; requirements of that jurisdiction must have been substantially equal to Indiana's at time of applicant's last registration/licensing; and the other jurisdiction must accord the same privilege to Indiana licensees. Applicant must be at least 18 years of age.
The other state must have a statewide plumbing code, the other state's examination must be at least equal to Kentucky's, and the other state must agree to reciprocate with Kentucky.

Temporary working permits for journeyman plumbers from states with like examinations, where that state recognizes the Louisiana license, or where other bona fide evidence shows the applicant's past experience would protect the public from defective plumbing. Temporary permits shall not be issued to master plumbers.
Applicant must pay fee, hold active equivalent license in good standing, meet MD qualifications, and the other state must offer similar reciprocal waiver to MD licensees

Applicants whose records are unavailable from a foreign country may apply for a reciprocal license with board and department approval by submitting notarized affidavit of education/experience and a notarized statement from a governmental official confirming unavailability of records. Military members/veterans/dependents with equivalent out-of-state licensure may also obtain licensure without examination.

Applicant must hold a valid comparable license in the qualifying state for at least one year; qualifying state must have statewide licensing program with examination and qualifying experience comparable to Minnesota's; applicant must not have failed the same or greater class exam in MN or had license revoked/suspended.

Applicant must be licensed in another state with substantially equivalent or greater standards, affirm verification request from other state, and not be subject to pending charges or final disciplinary action.
Satisfactory proof that qualifications are substantially equivalent to NC licensees, plus payment of the usual license fee. No written examination required.

Nonresident applicants must be registered under the laws of another state with substantially equivalent requirements, and that state must grant similar reciprocal privileges to North Dakota residents. Payment of the required fee is also required.
Equal reciprocity must be provided for NJ master plumbers by the applicant's home state, and that state's standards must be equal to or comparable to NJ's.

Reciprocal licensing agreement with states having equivalent licensing requirements; also expedited licensure available for military service members, veterans, and out-of-state licensees under the Uniform Licensing Act.

License by endorsement available for attainable housing projects in rural areas; applicant must hold a valid unrestricted license in another U.S. jurisdiction for at least 4 consecutive years, have no disciplinary history, pass a background check, and comply with bond and insurance requirements. A general license by endorsement program is also required under NRS 622.530.

Reciprocity available for backflow technicians under Chapter 4796 if the individual holds a license or certification in another state or has satisfactory work experience/government certification/private certification in a state that does not issue that certification.

Applicant must be currently licensed in another jurisdiction with substantially equivalent requirements, must have lawfully practiced the trade for 1 year immediately prior to application, must have no pending disciplinary matters, and the original license must have been obtained by examination.

Reciprocal agreement requires that the other state's standards, qualifications, and examinations for building trades and mechanical and specialty skills are substantially similar to Oregon's; issued without examination upon proof of out-of-state licensing and payment of fees.
Applicant must possess a certificate of license from another state with requirements equivalent to Rhode Island's journeyperson plumber requirements.

Nonresident applicant must be registered in another state with substantially equivalent requirements; payment of initial application fee, examination fee, and license fee required; no examination required.

Applicant must apply in the same manner as any other applicant, provide supporting documents, and hold an equivalent license in the other jurisdiction. Examination may be waived if applicant has held equivalent license for at least two years.

License by endorsement available if: (1) out-of-state license encompasses similar scope of practice; (2) at least one year of experience under that license; (3) license is in good standing. Division may also issue license based on substantially similar requirements or demonstrated competency.

Universal license recognition: must hold current valid license in another state for at least 3 years, other state required exam and standards, no pending investigations, good standing, no disqualifying criminal record, no discipline (except financial-only), and payment of fees.

Endorsement available for applicants licensed in good standing in another U.S. jurisdiction for at least 3 years. Traditional reciprocity also available where foreign state maintained equivalent standards and grants like exemption to VT licensees. Veterans who served as 12K Plumber with 8,000 hours/4 years may receive journeyman license without exam.

Applicant must be a registered journey level or specialty plumber in another state with substantially equivalent requirements, and that state must extend reciprocity to WA plumbers. Payment of appropriate fees required.

Person must hold a current equivalent license from another state (or city/town/village) with provisions the department determines are equivalent, OR have practical experience in another state the department determines is equivalent. A streamlined path exists for journeyman plumbers who completed an apprenticeship, passed a journeyman exam in another state, and practiced 5+ years under a substantially similar license without disciplinary actions.

fields.rationale: States cluster by how they frame plumbing scope: comprehensive pipe+fixture+drainage system lists, work-and-materials language, fixture/apparatus-focused shorthand, generic specialty-contractor language borrowed from contractor licensing, vague or minimal statutory text, or definitions centered on the person/role rather than the work.

"Plumbing" means the actual installation, repair, maintenance, alteration or extension of a plumbing system by any person.

"Plumbing" means the practice of and the materials and fixtures used in the installation, maintenance, extension, and alteration of all piping, fixtures, appliances, and appurtenances in connection with any of the following: (A) Sanitary drainage or storm drainage facilities, the venting system, and the public or private water supply systems, within or adjacent to any building or structure. "Master plumber" means any individual qualified under this chapter engaging in or about to engage in the business of installing plumbing or plumbing systems.

"Field of plumbing" means the business, trade, or work having to do with the installation, removal, alteration, or repair of plumbing and drainage systems or parts of plumbing and drainage systems.

fields.rationale: Values cluster by how strictly supervision is defined: physically present on-site with explicit presence rules, 'direct' supervision language without site-presence specifics, general/indirect supervision, states that carve out exceptions or tiered rules for advanced apprentices, and one state describing journeymen under masters rather than apprentices.

assignments.raw_value: An apprentice plumber must work directly under the supervision of a journeyman or master plumber.
An apprentice plumber must be supervised by a master plumber or journeyman plumber, except that a final-year apprentice may work under indirect supervision.
A licensed journeyman plumber, master plumber, or residential plumber may supervise apprentices at the job site.
Apprentice work may be performed only under the supervision of a licensed contractor or journeyman

An apprentice, journeyman, mechanic, or other person providing plumbing services must do so under the supervision of a master plumber who is the individual's employer or who is employed full time by the same business entity as the individual.
Journeyman plumbers install plumbing under the direction of a master plumber.
An apprentice or trainee learning the trade shall act under the supervision of a person appropriately licensed under this chapter
An apprentice must work under the supervision of a licensed journeyperson or master in the applicable discipline
Apprentices shall not perform plumbing work except under the supervision of a journeyman; specialty apprentices shall not perform specialty work except under supervision of a specialty journeyman.

Apprentice plumbers must perform all plumbing under the direct personal supervision of the sponsor or his or her agent, who must also be an Illinois licensed plumber. First and second year apprentices require direct personal supervision for all work except second-year maintenance and repair. All other apprentices require daily inspection after initial rough-in and after completion by the sponsor or agent.
An apprentice plumber must work under the direct and immediate personal supervision of a licensed plumbing contractor or a licensed journeyman plumber.
An apprentice must be under the personal supervision of a licensed master or licensed journeyman plumber.
Apprentices may engage in the art of plumbing only when they are under the direct, constant, on-the-job supervision of a licensed journeyman plumber.

An apprentice plumber must work under the direct supervision of a master plumber or journeyman plumber; an apprentice gas fitter under the direct supervision of a master plumber, master gas fitter, journeyman plumber, or journeyman gas fitter.
An apprentice plumber must work under the direction and control of a master plumber or holder of a limited master plumber license
A trainee plumber must work under the direct supervision of one or more licensed journeyman plumbers or licensed master plumbers.
An apprentice plumber must be supervised by a journey or master plumber with direct, on-site, in-person supervision.

A plumber's apprentice or registered unlicensed individual may assist in the installation of plumbing only while under the direct supervision of a master, restricted master, journeyworker, or restricted journeyworker plumber.
An apprentice must work under the personal direction and supervision of a licensed master plumber or a licensed journeyman plumber.
Apprentice plumbers must work under the supervision of a licensed plumber; a licensed master plumber may employ only apprentice plumbers registered with the state department of labor and industry.
A plumber's apprentice must work under the immediate and personal supervision of either a master or a journeyman plumber.
A journeyman plumber works under the supervision of a master plumber.
Employment of an apprentice working under the direct supervision of a certified journeyman is not prohibited by the Construction Industries Licensing Act.
A plumber's apprentice must work under the direct supervision of a licensed journeyman plumber or plumbing contractor.
An apprentice plumber may work at the trade of plumbing if the apprentice works under the supervision of a licensed journeyman plumber.
Apprentice plumbers must work under the direct supervision and instruction of a master plumber or journeyperson plumber.
A plumber's apprentice must work under the immediate and personal supervision of either a plumbing contractor or plumber.
A plumber's apprentice must work under the supervision of a responsible master plumber and the direct supervision of a licensed plumber.

A licensed apprentice plumber must be under the immediate supervision of a licensed master plumber, licensed residential master plumber, licensed journeyman plumber, or licensed residential journeyman plumber.
Individuals shall not be subject to licensure as a tradesman when working under the supervision of a tradesman who is licensed in the specialty for which work is being performed.
An apprentice plumber shall be supervised on the job by either a master or a journeyman plumber.

A trainee must be supervised by a journey level plumber, residential service plumber, or an appropriate specialty plumber who has an applicable certificate of competency. The supervising plumber must be on the same jobsite as the trainee for a minimum of seventy-five percent of each working day, or available via mobile phone with audio and visual direction under specified conditions.
Journeyman plumbers (restricted) and registered learners shall work under the supervision of a master plumber or a master plumber (restricted).
